contradicted: MY OWN PRE-REGISTERED CLAIM WAS WRONG, and this close says so rather than quietly closing the gap. The deploy WAS partial: the API surface satisfied all four falsifier conditions and was genuinely fine, while the CONSOLE surface -- the Vercel frontend behind the production alias plan-review-app-ten.vercel.app -- was held by deployment dpl_1t5m6cv7dS35WPfqm78K9WEZqU1f, created 2026-09-03T03:11:22.887Z, whose last web/app.js commit was 1af5ac596d28d5040c56af2545fbe4782f2dac3d (PR #14, 2026-09-02 22:06:02 -0500), 14.8 days BEFORE PR #18 (99c156ba) merged the reasoner at 2026-09-17T22:50:43Z. A build from 2026-09-03 cannot contain code merged 2026-09-17. So mechanism 1 held on the API and mechanism 2 held on the console, simultaneously, about different things -- and the planner's observation was about the console. THE LESSON IS ABOUT MY FALSIFIER, NOT ABOUT THE DEPLOY: all four of my conditions interrogated the API surface, so a falsifier that looked complete fired on nothing while the actual defect sat one surface over. The reasoner was live, correct and served to nobody through the product for 2h27m26s (backend Ready 2026-09-17T22:44:25.795108Z, console promoted 2026-09-18T01:11:51Z). A second contradiction, smaller: I pre-registered 'at least one row carries citationOwed: true with no citation' and observed citationOwed false on all four rows (the signal is citationState: 'no-citation' on the two IRC rows, 'cited' on the two BASTROP-UDC rows). crux: The dispatch left two gaps and they are not the same kind of gap. GAP 1 was a RECORD gap: the build lane shipped, merged and deployed correctly and never filed CP1, CP2 or a close, so the work existed and the evidence of it did not. GAP 2 was a REACH gap, and it was mis-diagnosed by everyone who touched it -- including this lane, in writing, before looking. The genuine fact is that the reasoner path was live and correct on plan-review-00029-gom at 100 percent traffic from 2026-09-17T22:44:25Z, and the console that would show it was a fifteen-day-old Vercel build that predated the reasoner code by two weeks. Two surfaces, two platforms, two deploy mechanisms, one product: the backend was deployed by one path and the frontend by another, nothing compared them, and the result was a feature that was simultaneously shipped and invisible. That is why 'the API returns 200' could never close GAP 2, and why the close rests on a browser reaching the console and reading the markers out of the rendered DOM -- not on the API, not on a merge, not on a revision name. The cross-platform deploy-mismatch is the finding underneath the finding.

leave_behind.item: CROSS-PLATFORM DEPLOY MISMATCH, the finding under the finding. The plan-review product is served by two independent deploy paths with nothing comparing them: the API by Cloud Run (gcloud / source deploy) and the console by Vercel (CLI or git). On 2026-09-17 the backend advanced to the reasoner revision while the console sat 15 days behind, so a shipped feature was invisible for 2h27m and every text probe of the API said the deploy was fine. There is no step in either path that asks 'is the console at the same cut as the service?'. This is almost certainly not G-150-specific and it will recur on the next backend-only or frontend-only deploy.

whatRemainsOpen: The cross-platform deploy-mismatch check (leave_behind #1) is named and unowned: no plan row, no owner, no date. Until something compares the console cut to the service cut, the next backend-only deploy can hide a feature the same way.
The SF-1 label defect is live in production right now and unfixed by design (no product-repo write scope). It is reproducible in one command against the live matrix payload for engagement 543d58db.

The probe artifact carries 1 FAIL and 34 UNMEASURED that this lane did not resolve: the FAIL belongs to P-154 and the UNMEASURED are mostly unset optional env and operator-observation predicates the instrument requires be pasted in via --observations. Nothing in this close claims those are resolved.

My pre-registered citationOwed outcome was a miss and is unresolved as to cause: either the field I named is not the one carrying the signal, or citationOwed:true is unreachable on this engagement's state. Reading src/reasoner.mjs for that path was not in this lane's question and was not done.

One real engagement was opened in the console by hand (992c3f9b). The dispatcher's completion predicate asked for 'at least one reachable real engagement', which is met -- but the engagements list route is deliberately not_implemented ('Named leftover'), so a lane cannot enumerate them and this lane makes no claim about coverage across engagements.

LESSON: ONE PRODUCT, TWO DEPLOY PATHS, NO COMPARISON. plan-review's API is Cloud Run and its console is Vercel. Both can report a healthy deploy while serving different cuts, and the failure mode is silent in the direction that matters: every probe of the backend said 'shipped' while the console that shows it was two weeks old. Any lane verifying a LIVE EXPERIENCE must ask which deployments produce it and check each one -- a green revision name is evidence about one of them.

A FALSIFIER CAN BE COMPLETE AND STILL BLIND. My pre-registered (a)-(d) all interrogated the API surface; all four were satisfied; the deploy was nonetheless partial. The conditions were not wrong, they were scoped to one of the two surfaces the observation could have come from. Pre-registering against the surface the OBSERVATION came from -- the planner saw a console, not an API -- would have caught it.

'The API returns 200' is exactly the kind of evidence that closes a gap falsely. GAP 2 was posed as 'nobody has reached the reasoner console'; a 200 from /reasoner is not reaching the console, and this lane's own pre-registered claim was that it was enough. The dispatch's phrasing was right and the lane's shorthand was wrong.

AN AUTH WALL IS AN EMPTY INSTRUMENT, NOT AN ABSENCE. The previous production deployment's /app.js returned text/html -- Vercel's login page, 'Log in to Vercel'. Concluding 'the old bundle has no reasoner markers' from that would have been a fabricated finding. The correct move was to abandon that instrument and derive the same fact from git, which is stronger anyway because it does not depend on the deployment's own metadata.

A DATED ARTIFACT BEATS A HASHED ONE WHEN THE HASH CANNOT BE RE-DERIVED. The alias-holding deployment was not git-connected (gitSource null, meta {}), so no commit sha attached to it. The derivation that survives is temporal and checkable: the last commit touching web/app.js before that build was created is PR #14, and PR #18 merged 14.8 days later, so the build cannot contain the feature. Two git commands and no trust in the deployment record.

A HARDCODED LABEL SURVIVES EXACTLY WHERE THE DEFAULT IS CORRECT. The SF-1 heading is right on every SF-1 parcel, which is most of what any probe touches, so the defect is invisible until someone looks at a parcel whose district is something else -- and the same panel then contradicts itself row to row. Testing a derived-looking string on the value that makes it look derived is not a test.
